title: fix: extend Wan 2.7 Replicate deadline
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Gives only `wan-pro` and `wan-pro-1080p` a 15-minute Replicate deadline; every other Replicate model remains at six minutes.
- Uses one deadline for `Cancel-After` and local polling, and maps deadline terminal states to 504.
- Raises the SDK default video timeout from 10 to 20 minutes so it can receive the Worker’s 15-minute response plus final media transfer.
- Keeps known input errors at 400 and capacity errors at 503 even when their messages contain timeout text.
- Keeps model IDs, aliases, prices, paid-only access, provider, capabilities, and no-fallback routing unchanged.

Paid local E2E passed 6/6 cache-miss probes across 720p/1080p, T2V/I2V, and 10/15-second output. The 15-second T2V jobs completed in 379s and 420s. Outputs were playable H.264/AAC; six misses deducted exactly 9.50 Pollen; an exact cache replay returned in 35ms without another provider charge.

Tradeoff: Replicate does not bill queued `aborted` predictions, but bills runtime for `canceled` predictions that already started; Pollinations cannot bill failed requests.

Checks: 27 focused tests, 711-test Gen suite, 30 SDK tests, both typechecks/builds, Biome, and diff check.

gist.headline: Wan gets more runway
gist.blurb: Long Wan 2.7 videos were arriving fashionably late to a six-minute deadline. Wan Pro and Wan Pro 1080p now get a full 15 minutes to finish their pixels, while the SDK waits long enough to bring the result home.
gist.summary: Extended Replicate deadlines for `wan-pro` and `wan-pro-1080p` from six to 15 minutes, aligned Worker cancellation and polling to that deadline, and raised the SDK video timeout from 10 to 20 minutes.
gist.impact: Long 10- and 15-second Wan 2.7 text-to-video and image-to-video jobs can now complete reliably, while input errors remain 400 and capacity errors remain 503 instead of being mistaken for timeouts.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Polli tending two especially tall Wan video-vines labeled Wan Pro and 1080p, with a friendly retro terminal showing a large 15-minute sand timer and a finished film reel. The longer runway should feel calm rather than urgent: video frames bloom from the vines while Polli watches the render patiently.
